verdict: OK to lend in Ludhiana fasteners — but only to units that can pass steel cost through; avoid price-takers selling to large OEMs on fixed-price contracts.
title: Ludhiana fasteners & hardware: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A fastener unit buys wire rod and steel, draws, cold-forges, threads, heat-treats and zinc-plates it into bolts, nuts and screws, and sells to auto OEMs, tractor makers, cycle and sewing-machine units and the hardware trade. **Cash is made on conversion spread, not on steel** — raw material is 50-55% of operating cost with steel the key input [8]. So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit has a price-reimbursement agreement with its key customers; if it sells on fixed-price annual contracts, ask who absorbs a steel spike.

## What has changed now
Steel prices have surged and industry bodies are asking for government intervention [1], and Punjab MSMEs are already feeling the squeeze on manufacturing growth [2]. Ludhiana's own industry has flagged steel prices under war strain [3]. **The cost line has moved against the borrower while selling prices lag.** Note the local sources are dated April and September 2026, so confirm current rod prices with the customer. The data pack is more encouraging: Punjab GST collections are up 9.7% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and IIP for NIC 25 output is up 16.9% YoY [D].

## Where the growth is
Peer results show the demand is real: Sterling Tools posted standalone revenue up ~32% YoY in Q2 FY27 [4], and Sundram Fasteners grew ~30% with exports up 57% [5]. **Pursue tier-2 auto and tractor fastener makers with export order books and pass-through clauses.** Avoid single-customer units selling to one large OEM on fixed prices, and traders holding steel inventory on borrowed money.

## How to grow safely
Structure term loans against self-funded capex, not against inventory revaluation. **Take monthly stock statements, a rod-price-linked drawing power and quarterly GST returns.** If drawing power is being propped up by steel price gains rather than volume, ask for the sales register.

## Early warning signs
- Monthly stock statement (monthly): inventory days rising while sales flat -> cut drawing power.
- GST returns (quarterly): turnover falling below the pre-spike run-rate -> ask for order book.
- Rod price tracker (weekly): sharp move with no price revision to customers -> seek customer confirmation of pass-through.
- Debtor ageing (monthly): OEM receivables past agreed terms -> reduce limit.
